title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: AI skill to investigate policy sync and device health
summary: The briefing accurately separates Microsoft's planned AI skill from today's documented device troubleshooting tools. Its rollout dates, Security Copilot capacity information and control paths are supported; the skill-specific controls, default and consumption rate remain documented gaps.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The notice's preparation steps ask admins to confirm SCUs are provisioned to support AI experiences.
claims.quote: Confirm that Security Compute Units are provisioned to support AI experiences.

claims.claim: Security Compute Units are the meter for Security Copilot AI compute.
claims.quote: A Security Compute Unit is a unit measure of the compute power to run Security Copilot workloads for AI capabilities within the standalone and embedded experiences.

claims.claim: The licensing model is consumption.
claims.quote: With the inclusion model, which provides 400 SCUs per 1,000 user licenses, there's no hourly provisioned capacity. Instead, the same two scenarios would deduct 3.5 SCUs from the monthly SCU allocation.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 inclusion provides 400 SCUs monthly for every 1,000 paid user licences.
claims.quote: Customers with Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 will have 400 Security Compute Units (SCU) each month for every 1,000 paid user license

claims.claim: The included monthly allocation is capped at 10,000 SCUs.
claims.quote: up to 10,000 SCUs each month at no additional cost.

claims.claim: That included allocation is supplied at no additional cost.
claims.quote: Customers with Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 will have 400 Security Compute Units (SCU) each month for every 1,000 paid user license, up to 10,000 SCUs each month at no additional cost.

claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Settings (gear icon in the upper right corner) > Device onboarding > Devices.

claims.quote: Go to the Microsoft Defender portal ... Navigate to Investigation & response > Hunting > Advanced hunting ... Sample query: DeviceInfo | where DlpInfo != "" | project DlpInfo

claims.claim: The device status UI and hunting query are existing read-only status and attribute views, not controls over the planned skill.
claims.quote: In addition to viewing device attributes in the Microsoft Purview portal, you can access the same Endpoint DLP device data through the DeviceInfo table in Advanced hunting.

claims.claim: The device health reporting dashboard is reached in Microsoft Purview at Settings > Device onboarding > Device report.
claims.quote: Go to the Microsoft Purview portal. Select Settings > Device onboarding > Device report.

claims.quote: To access the device health reporting dashboard, you must have one of the following roles: Compliance Administrator; Security Administrator; Global Administrator

claims.claim: Device readiness indicators identify risk of missing future policy updates, not confirmed failures.
claims.quote: These indicators don't confirm whether a device failed to receive a policy update, but instead highlight devices that may be at risk of not receiving future updates.

claims.claim: The Purview source is a general prerequisite for Security Copilot embedded experiences in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Security Copilot in Purview must be enabled for both the standalone and embedded experiences to work.

claims.quote: To enable or disable the Microsoft Purview source in Microsoft Security Copilot ... On the Manage plugins page, set the Purview toggle to On to enable or Off to disable.

claims.claim: The Devices list can take up to 2 hours to update Policy sync status.
